body.estimand_functional: \(M_{ij}=E_P[Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\) and \(U=\operatorname{left}_r(M)\).  The explicit hybrid \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\) satisfies \(c b_{nm}\le\inf_{\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}}\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\le\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)]\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\) in the lower-bound regime; separately, \(\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)]\le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\).

sampling_model.design: A triangular array of sequential randomized decisions ordered globally by \(o(i,j)=(i-1)m+j\), with filtration \((\mathbb G_k)_{k=0}^{nm}\) and explicit row baselines \(\mathcal F_{i,0}=\mathbb G_{(i-1)m}\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\) units observed at \(m\) ordered decision times, with bounded aspect ratio; the sharp experiment and Markov witness use \(n_\ell=2\ell\) and \(m_\ell=2\lceil\gamma\ell\rceil\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(A_{ij}\) is drawn with \(p_{ij}\in[q,1-q]\) given the global pre-cell field \(\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Recorded IPW--SVD uses the known predictable propensities and no estimated treatment nuisance.  Its matrix-Freedman guarantee is retained as \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\), but bounded outcomes and the signal floor make that radius nonshrinking at fixed complexity.  The observed-data hybrid switches deterministically to an incoherent sine frame when \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}>1\), yielding constant uniform risk without changing the law class.  The blind procedure replaces entrywise propensities by a clipped empirical row fraction and remains certified only at the nonshrinking \(d_{nm}\) resolution.  Simultaneous bands use direct recorded-IPW contrasts and deterministic variance envelopes; leave-one-cell-out multiplier exactness is not claimed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Published Theorem 1, equations (16b)--(17) on page 950, gives the rowwise upper bound, and Theorem 2, equation (22b) on page 953, gives the minimax lower bound under independent Bernoulli observation and independent noise.
Published Theorem 2.2 on page 1974 gives a Frobenius online-SGD rate and Theorem 3.1 on page 1977 gives fixed-form asymptotic normality for scalar rewards from independent Gaussian matrix contexts.
Published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389 bound nearest-neighbor error for each unit-by-time counterfactual mean under an adaptive pooled sequential policy.

Published Theorem 2 and equation (14) on page 1724 give a Frobenius RMSE upper bound for nuclear-norm completion of an untreated potential-outcome matrix when adoption dates are independent across units conditional on the latent matrix.

Published Theorem 3 in Section 4 of article e70002 gives a restricted-strong-convexity and Frobenius-error guarantee for the low-rank term estimated by the weighted MAR objective in equations (2) and (11).
Published Propositions 1--3 develop tall-wide factor imputation rates and limit laws for missing common components, with average and individual treatment effects on the treated as applications.

The published COLT extended abstract on pages 3821--3822 and its public full version give entrywise consistency and asymptotic normality for synthetic nearest neighbors under causal missing-not-at-random sampling.

Published Theorem 5 on page 2021 compares Frobenius upper bounds for known-propensity IPW and uniform-risk nuclear-norm completion under independent Bernoulli observation with a low-rank probability matrix.
The published article and its public full version develop groupwise nuclear-norm completion and debiased asymptotic normality for fixed block or staggered missing-not-at-random causal panels.

Public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 give a rowwise matrix-error upper bound for armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD under independent Bernoulli assignment and low-rank arm means.  Their rate has its own fourth-power logarithmic factor and shares only the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}\); \(b_{nm}\) additionally contains \(\sqrt{\log n}\) and the subspace conversion \(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm}\).
Published Theorem 3 and equation (10) on page 7 characterize variance improvement for a scalar adaptively normalized IPW estimator under independent treatment indicators.
Predictably weighted adaptive IPW scores yield scalar studentized martingale limits.
Balancing weights attain Frobenius guarantees and a lower bound under fixed heterogeneous missingness.
Debiased low-rank projection yields inference for a fixed linear form under independent sampling.

ArXiv Assumption 2 on pages 7--8 gives normalized third-moment, predictable-covariance, empirical-covariance, plug-in, growth, and variance-floor conditions under which Theorem 3.3 on page 8 validates simultaneous multiplier intervals for many martingale means.
Published Theorem 4 and equation (14) on page 348 validate a multiplier maximum for a coefficient matrix under modeled nonuniform missingness.

body.tldr: Recorded propensities identify the causal effect matrix and make entrywise IPW errors a bounded row-major martingale-difference array.  Write \(R_{nm}(\widetilde U)=\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\) and \(R^*_{nm}=\inf_{\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}}R_{nm}(\widetilde U)\).  In the stated lower-bound regime, the strongest same-assumption expected-risk result is now \(c b_{nm}\le R^*_{nm}\le R_{nm}(\widehat U^{\mathrm H})\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\le C\), where \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\) uses recorded IPW--SVD only when its deterministic loose radius is at most one and otherwise reports an incoherent discrete-sine frame.  Bounded outcomes force \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\) whenever the class is nonempty.  Consequently, at fixed complexity and bounded aspect ratio, \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\) but both \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and the blind resolution \(d_{nm}\) are at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\); their uniform guarantees are nonshrinking.  The adaptive witness rules out \(b_{nm}\)-attainment only for recorded IPW--SVD, so the minimax gap from \(b_{nm}\) to a constant remains open.  The rank-one \(0.25/0.75\) Markov law remains a blind-scaling stress design for HeartSteps II, and simultaneous dense-query radii retain a separate \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) multiplicity factor.

project_justification.gap: Published independent-mask rowwise matrix results do not settle causal effect-subspace risk under history-predictable assignment.  On the present effect-only low-rank class, a constant-propensity packing gives the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\).  The valid IPW--SVD radius is nonshrinking in every nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect regime, while a deterministic incoherent fallback reduces the uniform minimax upper endpoint to a constant.  The remaining gap is therefore from \(b_{nm}\) to constant order; the accepted IPW-specific obstruction does not supply an estimator-independent converse.
project_justification.niche: The contribution is an explicit expected maximum-row minimax bracket for a causal row subspace under predictable masks, with one admissible hybrid estimator attaining the constant endpoint, together with an estimator-specific IPW obstruction, a calibrated blind-normalization resolution theorem, and conservative simultaneous causal-contrast bands whose entropy cost is separate.
project_justification.fill: The project proves a \(b_{nm}\) constant-propensity minimax lower bound, a \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) moment guarantee for recorded IPW--SVD, and a deterministic-sine hybrid guarantee \(C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\le C\).  It derives the signal ceiling imposed by bounded outcomes and the resulting floors \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm},d_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n}\).  It retains the explicit Markov witness and the finite-sample direct-IPW simultaneous band with visible family-size inflation.

body.related_work:
Mehrotra, Tran, Vu, and Zampetakis analyze armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD under independent Bernoulli assignment and low-rank arm means.  For arm-mean matrices \(A^1\) and \(A^0\), the only algebraic implication used here is \(\operatorname{rank}(A^1-A^0)\le\operatorname{rank}(A^1)+\operatorname{rank}(A^0)\).  Its converse fails even for bounded matrices: with \(d=\min(n,m)\), take \(C=\varepsilon\sum_{k=1}^d e_k^{(n)}(e_k^{(m)})^\top\), \(D=\delta e_1^{(n)}(e_1^{(m)})^\top\), and \(0<\delta<\varepsilon\); then \(A^0=C\) and \(A^1=C+D\) are bounded and full rank \(d\), while \(A^1-A^0=D\) has rank one.  This witness establishes only failure of the converse rank implication, not containment between full statistical model classes or transfer of a rate.  Their public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 share only the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}\): their matrix-row bound has its own fourth-power logarithmic factor and armwise assumptions, whereas \(b_{nm}\) additionally has \(\sqrt{\log n}\) and the subspace conversion \(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm}\).

Cai, Li, Chi, Poor, and Chen give two-to-infinity upper and lower bounds for an independently sampled fixed low-rank matrix with independent noise; these inform the perturbation and packing architecture but do not resolve predictable causal subspace risk.  Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey support the recorded-propensity martingale-score reduction, and Tropp supplies the matrix Freedman inequality.  Dwivedi, Tian, Tomkins, Klasnja, Murphy, and Shah study adaptive nearest-neighbor arm-mean estimation under their exogenous factor conditions; their theorem has a different target and does not itself provide the present maximum-row minimax result.  Other completion and factor references concern Frobenius, entrywise, treated-cell, or fixed-missingness targets and are used only for context.

Khan and Ugander analyze scalar affine normalization under independent indicators; the blind row-fraction SVD and its \(0.25/0.75\) Markov witness are new objects here and do not refute that procedure.  Belloni and Oliveira and Ma, Niu, Zhang, and Zhu motivate high-dimensional martingale or multiplier inference, but the retained simultaneous theorem is a direct finite-sample Freedman and union-bound result.  Its \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) factor is a query-family entropy cost, not part of either subspace scale.  Spruijt-Metz et al. make saved propensities and omission sensitivity operationally relevant for the HeartSteps II consumer.

body.technical_internal_limitation: The frozen class allows target singular factors to depend on earlier outcomes, so rowwise leave-one-out arguments cannot treat them as predictable; the explicit obstruction shows this matters for recorded IPW--SVD.  The sine fallback removes the divergent normalized IPW upper endpoint but supplies only constant risk, leaving the estimator-independent gap \(b_{nm}\) to \(1\).  Nonemptiness plus bounded outcomes forces \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\); hence \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and the blind resolution \(d_{nm}\) are at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\) for fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\) and bounded aspect ratio.  The blind tangent and ratio expansion therefore give a coarse, nonshrinking uniform diagnostic in this regime.  Separate arm means in the denominator derivative are not estimable at a claimed frontier rate under effect-only low rank, and no residual covariance consistency, positive random studentizer, or feasible multiplier exactness is assumed.
body.honest_scope: Identification is given by the recorded-IPW conditional mean.  In the stated lower-bound regime, the proved common-risk statement is \(c b_{nm}\le R^*_{nm}\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\le C\), witnessed by one observed-data hybrid.  This is not a matched rate: the lower/reference scale can still vanish but, in a nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect regime, cannot be smaller than order \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\), while the available uniform upper endpoint is constant.  Recorded IPW--SVD separately has the \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) moment bound and an estimator-specific \(b_{nm}\)-scale failure witness; neither implies constant-order risk for every observed-data estimator.  The blind procedure is certified only at nonshrinking \(d_{nm}\) resolution, and the \(0.25/0.75\) Markov sequence is a boundary example for that procedure and a HeartSteps II stress design.  Simultaneous inference uses conservative direct-IPW radii with separate query-family multiplicity, not feasible multiplier exactness.  Comparator discussion uses only the one-way armwise rank inequality and an explicit bounded full-rank common-component counterexample to its converse; it makes no model-containment or rate-transfer claim.
